diagnostic_evidence.quote: \# of samples $N_s$   &  $1$ if noise-free; $100$ if noisy

issues.failure_explanation: MSTD is defined as the average over test pairs of the norm of the empirical standard deviation across the N_s generated samples, divided by N_s. The stated testing protocol uses a single sample for all noise-free evaluations ('$N_s$: $1$ if noise-free' in Table tab:params-test2; '$N_s$: $1$ in tab:params-test3/tab:params-test4). With N_s = 1 the empirical std over one sample is identically 0 (or undefined under Bessel's correction), so the defined MSTD is 0/undefined for every noise-free test case -- yet Tables tab:darcy_error, tab:burgers, tab:adv_error report nonzero MSTDs (e.g., 5.08e-07, 5.47e-04, 7.91e-04). Additionally, dividing the pointwise std by N_s makes the metric shrink with the number of samples even for a fixed learned distribution, so as defined it does not measure a 'mean standard deviation'. The reported MSTD values are therefore irreproducible from the stated definition and protocol.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the actual protocol used to estimate the standard deviation (a number of samples N_s > 1 for the noise-free runs, consistent with the 'diagnostic run' described in the text), remove or justify the division by N_s in the MSTD definition, and re-verify the tabulated MSTD values.
issues.overall_effect: The MSTD columns of Tables tab:darcy_error, tab:burgers, and tab:adv_error, and the diagnostic claim that the learned noise-free conditional distribution has 'approximately zero' standard deviation, are unsupported as written. The MRLE values and all accuracy comparisons are unaffected.
issues.title: MSTD definition and stated sample counts cannot produce the reported values
issues.why_classification: The defect is a local inconsistency between a metric definition, the reported sample counts, and the tabulated numbers; correcting the evaluation description is a short local fix with no change to the method, the MRLE results, or the advertised scope, so every substantive claim survives.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Suppose that the initial state $u_0$ follows a (nonzero mean) Gaussian distribution with the identity covariance, i.e., $u_0 \sim \mathcal{N}(m, \mathbf{I})$
after integrating out $u_0$ in~\eqref{eqn:true-reverse}, the true reverse distribution $p(u_{t-1} | u_t)$ has a covariance $\beta_t \mathbf{I}$
Note that we do not assume the covariance $\Sigma(a)$ is known
The model is trained on the noisy data set with $\sigma=0.0005$.

issues.failure_explanation: The optimality claim for the 'additive Gaussian noise' branch of eqn:cov rests on Proposition prop:added-2, whose hypothesis is that the data conditional on a have identity covariance, u_0 ~ N(m, I); only under that hypothesis does integrating out u_0 yield the true reverse covariance beta_t I and the entropy equality H_p(u_{t-1}|u_t) = H_{q_theta}(u_{t-1}|u_t) for Sigma_theta = beta_t I. The paper's noisy-data model is u_eta = u + eta with eta ~ N(0, Sigma(a)), Sigma(a) unknown, and the noisy experiments use noise levels far from unit variance (sigma = 1%, 5% in Test 1 on unnormalized data; sigma = 0.0005, 0.001 in Test 2). For conditional covariance sigma^2 I the forward chain gives Var(u_{t-1}|u_t) = beta_t (1 - bar_alpha_{t-1}(1-sigma^2))/(1 - bar_alpha_t(1-sigma^2)) I, which equals beta_t I only when sigma^2 = 1 and tends to the noise-free branch ((1-bar_alpha_{t-1})/(1-bar_alpha_t)) beta_t I as sigma^2 -> 0. Hence in the regime where the paper applies it, the asserted optimality is false -- by the paper's own entropy criterion the noise-free branch would be near-optimal instead -- and the bridging sentence 'A similar result holds in the case of data perturbed by an additive Gaussian noise' overgeneralizes prop:added-2 beyond its hypothesis.

failure_location.quote: Hence, the parameterization~\eqref{eqn:cov} for $\Sigma_{\theta}$ in the Gaussian noise setting is optimal in the sense that $H_p(u_{t-1}|u_t) = H_{q_{\theta}}(u_{t-1}|u_t)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the optimality statement to the unit-noise-variance case (stating the hypothesis explicitly) and present Sigma_theta = beta_t I as a heuristic choice for general Sigma(a); alternatively, generalize Proposition prop:added-2 to u_0 ~ N(m, sigma^2 I) and adopt the resulting sigma^2-dependent optimal covariance in eqn:cov.
issues.overall_effect: The stated information-theoretic justification of the noisy-data branch of eqn:cov -- the reverse covariance used in all noisy-data experiments -- is invalid for the paper's noise model and experimental regime; the optimality claim and the closing 'exact likelihood' entropy equality for the Gaussian-noise case are unsupported there. The PDNO algorithm itself and all reported empirical results are unaffected.
issues.title: Optimality justification for the noisy-data reverse covariance applies only to unit-variance noise
issues.why_classification: The covariance choice is an auxiliary heuristic component: a one-sentence qualification (unit-variance assumption) or a contained re-derivation makes the statements correct while the method, the experimental conclusions, and the advertised scope all survive unchanged, requiring no new nontrivial argument and causing no substantive loss.
